Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:1.english: With fleeces of wool - Shearings of wool:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:2.english: And wineskins of wine - leather bottles of wine:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:3.hebrew: בירא מתתאי - במורד ההר, למטה מבורו של אשמדאי:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:3.english: A pit lower down - On the slope of the mountain, below Ashmedai's pit:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:4.hebrew: ושפינהו למיא - כגון "השופה יין לחמריה" (ב"מ דף ס:) — הריק מי בור העליון לתוך התחתון דרך נקב שנקב בשפה שבין שתי הבורות, ומתוך שהראשון קרקעיתו גבוהה מקרקעית התחתון, נרוקו המים לתוכו מאליהן:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:4.english: And he drained the water - [This is] like [the expression], "one who pours off wine [from one vessel to another]" (Bava Metzia 60b) — he emptied the water of the upper pit into the lower [pit] through a hole that he bored in the wall between the two pits, and since the floor of the first [pit] was higher than the floor of the lower [pit], the water emptied into it on its own.

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:5.hebrew: וסתמינהו - לנקבים שבין זה לזה, כדי שכשישים יין בעליון לא יזוב ממנו לתחתון:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:5.english: And he plugged them - [namely,] the holes between this [pit] and that [one], so that when he puts wine in the upper [one], it will not flow from it into the lower [one]:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:6.english: And he dug a pit - another [pit], above Ashmedai's pit:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:7.hebrew: וטמינהו - מילא אותן שתי בורות עפר, כדי שלא יבין אשמדאי:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:7.english: And he covered them up - He filled those two pits [with] earth so that Ashmedai would not notice:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:8.hebrew: טמינהו - סתמן, כדמתרגמינן "סתמום פלשתים" (בראשית כ״ו:ט״ו): "טמנון פלישתאי":
Rashi on Gittin 68a:10:8.english: He plugged them [taminhu] - [This means] he stopped them up, just as we translate [in Aramaic for] "the Philistines stopped them up" (Genesis 26:15): "tamnun Pelishta'ei":

Rashi on Gittin 68a:11:2.english: He checked his seal - and found it intact:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:11:3.english: He was unable [to bear it] - he could not restrain himself:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:11:4.english: He became intoxicated and slept - [meaning] he got drunk and fell asleep:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:12:1.english: He descended, [and] came - Benayahu [descended] from the tree:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:12:2.english: He enclosed him - He closed the chain around his neck so that his head could not come out:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:12:3.english: He was struggling - [He was] acting wildly and exerting himself to tear it [the chain] off from himself:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:12:4.english: Of your Master - the Holy One, Blessed be He:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:13:1.english: He rubbed against it - He rubbed himself against it:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:13:2.hebrew: כובא - צריף קטן, כמו כובא דציידי:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:13:2.english: Kuva - A small hut, like a hunter's hut [kuva detzayadei]:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:13:3.english: Of a widow - A widow was living in it:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:1:1.hebrew: איגניב לן כסא דכספא - שהיו רואים אותו כרך בסודריה, ורוצין לבדוק מהו:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:1:1.english: A silver cup was stolen from us - [They said this] because they saw that bundle in his scarf, and wanted to check what it was:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:1.english: They said to him - to the Exilarch:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:2.english: Of white [spots] - Meat of [an animal] afflicted with boils:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:3.english: I ate and I tasted - I tasted:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:4.english: A white [animal] was not prepared for us today - We did not slaughter an animal afflicted with boils today:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:5.hebrew: בדוכתא - בעור היו בודקין, במקום ריסתנא זו בכף הירך, ותמצאנו בעור שהוא לבן:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:5.english: In the place - They would check the skin, at the place of this portion [of meat] on the hollow of the thigh, and you will find on the skin that it is white:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:6.hebrew: דאמר רב חסדא חיורא באוכמתא לקותא היא - טלאי לבן בעור שחור — לקותא היה שם בבשר, ונהפך העור ללבן:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:2:6.english: As Rav Chisda said: White in black is an affliction - A white patch on black skin — there was an affliction there in the flesh, and the skin turned white:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:1.english: They dug a pit for him - They dug a pit so that he would fall into it:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:2.english: And they threw a mat [tzifta] for him - They threw a reed mat over the mouth of the pit so that he would not discern his seat:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:3.english: Let the master come [and] rest - to lie down on his bed:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:4.hebrew: נחר ליה רב חסדא - עשה לו סימן, כמו "נחרת סוסיו" (ירמיהו ח):
Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:4.english: Rav Chisda snorted to him - He made a sign to him, like "the snorting of his horses" (Jeremiah 8[:16]):

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:5.hebrew: א"ל - רב ששת לינוקא, "פסוק לי פסוקיך":
Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:5.english: He said to him - Rav Sheshet [said] to a child, "Recite your verse for me":

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:6.english: Turn [aside] - It is a verse concerning Asahel:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:3:7.english: Turn away from it - Turn back from it to the right or to the left:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:5:1.english: Pools - to bathe in them in cold [water]:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:5:3.english: Sheidah and sheidtin - A male demon and a female demon.

Rashi on Gittin 68a:5:4.english: Shiddeta - A shidda [is] a carriage for the riding of women and princes:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:6:2.hebrew: מה היא - מה דמותה ומה טיבה; ויש אומרים: שידה עצמה, ראש כולן ואמן, איני יודע מאי היא:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:6:2.english: What it is - [meaning] what its form is and what its nature is; and some say: [a *sheidah*] herself [is] the head of all of them and their mother, [and] I do not know what she is:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:7:1.english: How shall I do [it] - without iron tools:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:7:2.hebrew: שמיר - בריה מששת ימי בראשית, ואין כל דבר קשה יכול לעמוד מפניו:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:7:2.english: Shamir - [It is] a creature from the six days of Creation, and nothing hard can withstand it.

Rashi on Gittin 68a:7:3.hebrew: לאבני אפוד - דאמרינן במסכת סוטה (דף מח:): אבנים הללו אין כותבין עליהם בדיו, שנאמר: "פתוחי חותם", ואין מסרטין עליהם באיזמל, שנאמר: "במלואתם" — שלא יהו חסרות כלום; אלא כותב עליהם בדיו ומראה להן שמיר מבחוץ, והן נבקעות מאליהן:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:7:3.english: For the stones of the ephod - For we say in Tractate Sotah (48b): These stones are not written upon with ink [alone], as it is stated: "Like the engravings of a signet," nor are they incised with a chisel, as it is stated: "In their settings" — [meaning] that they must not be lacking anything; rather, one writes upon them with ink and shows them the shamir from the outside, and they split open on their own:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:8:1.english: He subdued them - He compelled them with torments to tell him where it [the shamir] is:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:8:2.hebrew: כבשינהו - לחצן, לשון מכבש של בגדים (שבת דף קמא.):
Rashi on Gittin 68a:8:2.english: [He] pressed them - he squeezed them, [from the same] expression [as] a garment press (Shabbat 141a):

Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:1.english: Where is he - Ashmedai, so that I may subdue him:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:2.english: On such-and-such a mountain - on a certain mountain:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:3.english: He dug a pit for himself - He dug a pit there for himself:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:5.english: And sealed it with his gushpankeih - with his seal:

Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:6.hebrew: סייר לגושפנקיה - בודקו, שלא נגע אדם בו לגלות בורו:
Rashi on Gittin 68a:9:6.english: He checks his seal - He inspects it [to ensure] that no one has touched it to uncover his pit:

Tosafot on Gittin 68a:11:1.hebrew: וכתיב זנות ויין ותירוש - אף על פי שזה הפסוק לא נכתב עדיין, היו יודעין, כמו "ארור עושה מלאכת ה' רמיה", בפ' לא יחפור (ב"ב דף כא:) גבי יואב:
Tosafot on Gittin 68a:11:1.english: And it is written: Harlotry, wine, and new wine - Even though this verse had not yet been written, they knew [it], like [the verse] “Cursed be he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully,” in the chapter [entitled] Lo Yachpor (Bava Batra 21b) regarding Joab:

Tosafot on Gittin 68a:2:1.hebrew: דאמר רב חסדא אוכמא בחיורא וחיורא באוכמא לקותא היא - פירוש: טלאי שחור בעור לבן או טלאי לבן בעור שחור, אין זה אלא מחמת נגע שהיה שם. הקשה רבינו תם, דבנזיר בריש פרק בית שמאי (נזיר דף לא:) משמע דלא מיירי רב חסדא אלא בשור שחור בין שוורים לבנים, שהשחור מגרע כולם ומתקלקל מקחם על ידו; ופריך התם ממתני' דהתם, דמשמע שהלבן גרוע, ומסיק דרב חסדא איירי בתורא דקרמנאי, דהתם שחור גרוע טפי. ואור"ת דתרי מילי נינהו, ומילתיה דהכא איירי בטלאי שחור בעור לבן ולבן בעור שחור, והתם מיירי בשור שחור בין שוורים לבנים. ותדע, דבכל הספרים ישנים לא גרסינן התם במילתיה דרב חסדא אלא "אוכמא בחיורא לקותא", ותו לא. וכן נראה, דאי גרסינן תרווייהו כמו הכא, ונפרש חד לטלאי וחד לשור בין השוורים, אם כן מאי פריך התם? דמנא ליה ד"אוכמא בחיורא" קאי אשור בין השוורים? נימא איפכא, ולא יקשה כלום. רבינו תם:
Tosafot on Gittin 68a:2:1.english: As Rav Ḥisda said: Black within white and white within black is an affliction - Meaning: a black patch on white skin or a white patch on black skin — this is only because of a blemish that was there. Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: in Nazir, at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (Nazir 31b), it is implied that Rav Ḥisda is speaking only of a black ox among white oxen, for the black [ox] detracts from all of them and their sale is spoiled because of it; and [the Gemara] there raises an objection from the Mishnah there, which implies that the white [ox] is inferior, and it concludes that Rav Ḥisda is speaking of Carmanian oxen, for there the black [ox] is more inferior. And Rabbeinu Tam answers that they are two [separate] statements: his statement here speaks of a black patch on white skin and white on black skin, whereas there it speaks of a black ox among white oxen. And know [that this is so], for in all the old manuscripts we do not read there in Rav Ḥisda's statement anything other than "black among white is an affliction," and nothing more. And so it appears [to be], for if we read both [clauses] like here, and we explain one as referring to a patch and one as referring to an ox among oxen, then what is [the Gemara] asking there? For how does it know that "black among white" refers to an ox among oxen? Let us say the reverse, and nothing would be difficult! [From] Rabbeinu Tam:

Tosafot on Gittin 68a:7:1.hebrew: איכא שמיר דאייתי משה לאבני אפוד - הכא משמע דלאבני אפוד בעי שמיר, ובפ"ק דקידושין (דף לא.), גבי עובדא דדמא בן נתינה, בקשו ממנו אבנים לאפוד, וזה היה בבית שני, מדקאמר "לשנה נולדה לו פרה אדומה כו'", דבבית ראשון לא עשו פרה, כדאמר: "שניה עשה עזרא"; ואם כן, היה שמיר בבית שני. ואין להקשות דבפרק בתרא דסוטה (דף מח.) תנן: "משמתו נביאים הראשונים בטלו אורים ותומים, ומשחרב בית המקדש בטל שמיר" — דהיינו בית המקדש שני, מדנקט "בית המקדש" סתם, והתם בגמרא נקט "בית המקדש ראשון" על מילי אחריני; ועוד, מדלא ערבינהו בהדי אורים ותומים, והוי ליה למיתני "משמתו נביאים הראשונים בטלו אורים ותומים והשמיר", ד"משמתו נביאים הראשונים" היינו משחרב בית המקדש ראשון בטלו אורים ותומים. וצריך לומר ששמרוהו מימי שלמה עד חורבן בית שני. הקשה ה"ר אלחנן במסכת ע"ז בפ' ר' ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף נב:), גבי אבני מזבח ששקצום אנשי יון: "ליתברינהו? אבנים שלמות אמר רחמנא! לינסרינהו? לא תניף עליהם ברזל אמר רחמנא!" — ולינסרינהו ע"י שמיר! ואומר ר"י דע"י שמיר אין נעשין חלקות, דחגירת צפורן פוסלת במזבח. והך סוגיא אתיא כמ"ד בסוטה (דף מח:) דאיצטריך שמיר לאבני בית המקדש, והא דכתיב "מגוררות במגירה" מוקי לה באבני ביתו:
Tosafot on Gittin 68a:7:1.english: There is a shamir that Moses brought for the stones of the ephod - Here it implies that for the stones of the ephod, the shamir is needed. And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (31a), regarding the incident of Dama ben Netina, they sought stones for the ephod from him; and that was during the Second Temple, since [the Gemara] says, "The next year a red heifer was born to him, etc.," for in the First Temple they did not prepare a red heifer, as [the Gemara] says, "Ezra prepared the second [red heifer]" — and if so, the shamir existed during the Second Temple. And one should not object [from the fact] that in the last chapter of Sotah (48a) we learned in a Mishnah: "When the earlier prophets died, the Urim and Tumim ceased, and when the Temple was destroyed, the shamir ceased" — for that refers to the Second Temple, since it states "the Temple" unspecified, whereas there in the Gemara it mentions "the First Temple" regarding other matters; and furthermore, since it did not group them together with the Urim and Tumim — for it should have taught: "When the earlier prophets died, the Urim and Tumim and the shamir ceased," since "when the earlier prophets died" means that when the First Temple was destroyed, the Urim and Tumim ceased. And one must say that they preserved it from the days of Solomon until the destruction of the Second Temple. Rabbi Elchanan raised a difficulty in tractate Avodah Zarah, in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 52b), regarding the stones of the altar that the Greeks defiled: [the Gemara asks:] "Let them break them? The Merciful One said 'whole stones'! Let them saw them? The Merciful One said 'you shall not lift up iron upon them'!" — [Rabbi Elchanan asks:] So let them saw them by means of the shamir! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that by means of the shamir they are not made smooth, for a notch [that catches] a fingernail disqualifies [a stone] for the altar. And this sugya [here] follows the one who says in Sotah (48b) that the shamir was needed for the stones of the Temple, and that which is written "sawed with a saw" he establishes as referring to the stones of his [own] house:

Tosafot on Gittin 68a:8:1.english: Go bring a male demon, etc. - Because they did not want to inquire of the Urim and Thummim when they could inquire through something else:
